question: What necessary size bound do complete one/two-sign words and original-word initial branches impose on ANY nontrivial freely uniquely decodable fixed letter code, without prefix or suffix freedom?
contract: One finite code C of distinct nonempty finite working-unit strings, one code per abstract sourceletter. Arbitrary sequences of codewords are uniquely decodable (UD). Prefix/suffix freedom is NOT required. Whole native groups are complete concatenations in C*. A longer code must actually be used. No contextual code, erased/zero entry, per-word codebook, unmarked spelling alias, native atom/boundary correction or source grammar used to disambiguate a nonUD code. No length cap.
selection: Exactly all immutable1233eligible occurrences, separate readers. Let A be22fixed working units; verify every unit occurs. W unique complete unit strings. W1 length1, W2 length2. No native quotient strings enter the new proof.
enumeration: Enumerate every exact singleton subset S of A containing W1. S=A is identity only and kept separately, never a nontrivial positive. For each proper S, B(S) consists of its singletons plus every whole ab in W2 for which a or b is absent from S. These digrams must be individual codewords, since their only other nonempty factorization is a|b. A nonUD B(S) forbids any containing UD C. Decide B using complete finite residual search, retaining a collision or closed residual certificate.
capacity: For each h outside S, d_h counts DISTINCT second units of ORIGINAL full h-initial words; b_h counts already forced h-headed B entries. At least d_h h-headed codes are needed because singleton h is absent. Lower L(S)=|B|+sum(max(0,d_h-b_h) for h outside S), then max(L,|S|+1). The latter uses all A occurring and S proper. Longer h-codes with h INSIDE S remain legal and must never be banned; the bound optimistically ignores any additional cost. Minimize over every proper S with UD B. Necessary bound only, no global minimum or full C existence.
cap_meaning: Generic entry-count reference points, not identified source alphabets. Below bound EXCLUDED_NONTRIVIAL; otherwise NOT_EXCLUDED. No viable properS implies only identity. No positive full-word code or decoder follows.
optional_consequence: Intersection of every short-code-compatible proper S plus identity gives signs forced singleton by this necessary test alone. No1234forced set imported. If no proper S remains, allAforced. This statement concerns all possible sizes, not a cap-filtered subset.
fixtures: Before target enumerate all UD codebooks from binary nonempty strings length<=3 using independent residual-set checker. For all455sets of1..3binary words length<=3 containing both letters, parse exactly with dynamic programming, and check required B membership and capacity against every compatible actual code using a longer entry. Six named cases include nonprefix UD {a,ab}, forced-middle conflict a/c/ab/bc, positive repeated aa/b, and AAA/b with a possible3-unit code.
validation: Independent nonimporting validator derives every S/B and input summary anew, uses separate unoriented residual closure, checks each collision concatenation or complete residual set, recomputes all missing-head counts/lower bounds and exhaustiveness across all proper S. Immutable1233input hash and original eligibility validation retained. No new mixed TSV or image query.

human_motivation: A reader may inspect the whole written word before separating its letters, instead of recognizing each letter instantly from its left edge. This is a generous capacity class, not proof all UD codes are easy to learn or historically attested. A future practical writer still owes a small public decoding rule.
assumptions: Exact whole-group boundaries preserve sourceword boundaries
Fixed22working atoms; no physical atomicity proof
Free UD over arbitrary letter sequences, stronger than grammar-assisted recognition
All old rare readings retained and readers separate; no independent holdout

decisions.bound_exceeds_cap: Stop that entire size-limited nontrivial UD letter-channel class under these assumptions, including both prefix/suffix subsets.
